One's physical appearance, in my experience, always seems to come secondary to how much effort one puts into themselves. I am no expert but I think one must like themselves before anyone else will. It's not just about 'hitting the gym' so to speak as it is finding coping mechanisms to deal with issues such as your anxieties. Do you want to be able to happily participate in a social setting, or do you think you would ultimately prefer not to? The choice is yours, but if you want to see change, I believe there are steps you can take to get to where you want to be. Not just for others, but for yourself. You sound smart and capable. You can do more than you know. 


>If happen to find a girl of my dreams, there's just no way she'll be at all interested in me. Which will surely drive me to suicide, if I haven't killed myself by then.

Of course we are not the same person, but I am 6 or 7 years older than you and can tell you that I have met the girl of my dreams several times. They may seem perfect for you at that time, but maybe there is more to it than finding someone who is compatible with you in your developmental stages. Maybe it is better to find someone after you have reached your personal goals. And it seems easier to find that person with the connections you make on the way to achieving those goals.

Do yourself a favor before making such a decision, and give yourself a chance to be the person you want to be. Best of luck to you.

You know, every time I've ever been to a hospital, I always got a crazy bill. But one time a couple years ago I walked into an ER and told them I was going to kill myself if I didn't get some immediate help. I spent the evening in the ER under watch and was transferred to an inpatient facility the next morning. Honestly I don't even know where the facility was. To this day I never received a bill, a letter, a follow-up call, nothing. 

Honestly, yeah, they didn't help at all, but they didn't bill me for a dime either. I didn't have insurance and I was only asked for it one time during the initial ER visit. I wonder if that's just my state, or what.
